Ministerio de Economía
footnotes: In 2015, the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries made the first estimate on food losses and waste in Argentina, where seven food sectors were prioritized (meat -beef, poultry and pork-, cereals -wheat and corn-; fruits -pepita, stone fruit and citrus;  milk; oilseeds -soybean and sunflower-; and potato).  The methodology used for the estimation of Argentina's baseline took as a reference the study conducted by the Swedish Institute of Food and Biotechnology (SIK) for the FAO (2011), in which a global measurement of food loss and waste was made. Conversion factors were established based on sources and informants in each sector, while the allocation factors and proportions of fresh and processed fruits and vegetables were derived and processed fruits and vegetables were derived from local sources by product group. The data is published in: https://alimentosargentinos.magyp.gob.ar/HomeAlimentos/PDA/documentos/PDA_ejercicio_de_estimacion.pdf

records.source_detail: Ministerio de Economía
footnotes: This data is from Autonomous City of Buenos Aires in 2017, which presents 3 million inhabitants in total. This study was conducted through the application of a survey to a statistically representative sample of households in the city. This is the only relevant study carried out in Argentina on the estimation of food waste in households. The data is published in: https://buenosaires.gob.ar/alimentos/datos-y-estadisticas

records.source_detail: Ministerio de Economía
footnotes: The data represent the self-chain sector (mass consumption channel corresponding to supermarket chains). The study achieved the participation of 41% of supermarkets in terms of market share of sales. Detailed and validated information was compiled for the supermarket sector which, projected on the total sales of the market, covers 100% of supermarkets and self-service stores and, on the basis of the 41% participating, makes it possible to project the analysis of the market share of supermarkets and self-service stores.The waste that originates from food intended for sale in the channel, but that does not end up in human consumption, regardless of the cause, was determined. The data corresponds to the operational waste that relates to the phenomenon generated by the commercial operation, including storage and distribution generated in the supermarket chains.  The data is published in: https://alimentosargentinos.magyp.gob.ar/HomeAlimentos/PDA/pdf/Desperdicio-de-alimentos-en-supermercados-y-autoservicios-de-Argentina-Causas-y-estimaciones.pdf

records.source_detail: Ministerio de Economía
footnotes: For this new estimation of food waste in self chains, the Secretary with GS1 Argentina, the support of UNEP and other organizations, developed a Dashboard using supermarkets real data of food waste. The participation rate in the calculation of food waste by supermarket chains represents 61% of the self-chain segment, which leads to a market estimate of 24.4% at the national level. The data is published in: https://alimentosargentinos.magyp.gob.ar/HomeAlimentos/PDA/pdf/Desperdicio-de-alimentos-en-supermercados-y-autoservicios-de-Argentina-2022.pdf
